html:
One of the largest peoples of Africa, living mainly in southeastern Nigeria, east of the lower Niger River. They speak Igbo, a language of the Niger-Congo family.

The bronzes from Igbo-Ukwu, made in about the 800s or 900s, are the earliest firm trace of their ancestors' society, and show skilled metalwork and long-distance trade. Much of Igboland had no kings. Villages were run by councils of elders, age groups and title societies, and people often say "Igbo enwe eze", "the Igbo have no king". The town of Nri held religious authority over a wide area.

In the era of the Atlantic slave trade the Aro traders, backed by their famous oracle, ran a network that sent many captives to the coast. Huge numbers of Igbo were shipped through the Bight of Biafra. Olaudah Equiano, who wrote one of the first slave narratives, said he was born Igbo.

Britain conquered the region around 1900. In the Aba Women's War of 1929 Igbo women rose against colonial taxes and chiefs. Igbo people took up mission schooling and trade and spread across Nigeria. After massacres in the north in 1966, the east broke away as Biafra in 1967; the war and the Biafran famine killed somewhere between half a million and two million people. Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart tells of an Igbo village meeting colonial rule, and Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie has written of the Biafran war.
sum: One of the largest peoples of Africa, living mainly in southeastern Nigeria, east of the lower Niger River. They speak Igbo, a language of the Niger-Congo family.
